new.description: XNU as a loadable kernel module inside Linux (macOS personality for arm64 Linux)
new.readme: Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it. xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel module (xnu.ko) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module (fki.ko).

items.title: Freight and payables teams can self-host invoice agents with OCR off the GPU
items.connection: OCRia pulls text and layout from pages on one CPU core, so Ling-3.2-air spends its 5.5B active parameters only on reasoning and workflow steps, and Univer gives clerks an agent-editable spreadsheet for the results inside the team's own product.
items.context: many finance teams cannot send supplier documents to third-party APIs
chain: OCR moves off the GPU, at about 426 ms per page on a single CPU core.
The GPU budget goes only to Ling-3.2-air, which activates 5.5B of 124B parameters per token and has day-0 vLLM support and ready quants.
One modest self-hosted box can extract, match and flag exceptions on invoices and shipping documents, with results written into Univer sheets clerks already know how to edit.
Mid-size shippers can drop per-page OCR API fees and keep supplier data in house, which turns a compliance blocker into a cost saving.
items.who: Accounts payable and freight audit teams at mid-size shippers benefit; finance operations budgets or the consultants who build these flows pay.
items.versus: It beats paid OCR plus a hosted LLM because pages never leave the network and per-page fees go away, and it beats doing nothing because clerks retype less.
items.smallest_test: Run 200 past invoices through OCRia then Ling-3.2-air on one GPU; success if at least 90% of header fields match the ERP record and the pipeline outpaces the current clerk rate.
items.disconfirm: OCRia's output loses table structure, so Ling-3.2-air misreads line items more often than when given the page images directly.

items.body: LlamaIndex's open OCR model reads text and layout at about 426 ms per page on one CPU core, so ingestion needs no GPU or paid API. Ling-3.2-air can then reason over those documents and run workflow steps while activating only 5.5B of its 124B parameters per token, with day-0 vLLM support. Not yet shown: OCR accuracy against larger models, and an outside check of the team's AutomationBench-AA gain from 15.7% to 61%.

items.lead: Anthropic says an internal Claude model produced a machine-checked proof that VP differs from VNP over every field.
items.body: Anyone can inspect the 70-page paper and its Lean formalization instead of taking the claim on trust. If it holds, frontier math results may start arriving with proofs a computer has already checked. Expert review is not reported yet, and the result does not settle P vs NP.

items.lead: The harness around a model is becoming the part teams tune.
items.body: The robot policy study argues that interface design, not just model choice, decides whether a general model can control a robot, though its success rates are the authors' own and no code is linked. The backend switcher makes the same bet for coding agents, letting teams change the model under a tool without changing the tool, but its stars show interest, not output quality.
